h1: The 7 Best Inkjet Printers for Home Use of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Home Inkjet Printers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best inkjet printers for home use, comparing cartridge and ink-tank models on running cost, features, and setup.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is our top pick for homes that print regularly, with a refillable ink-tank design. The HP Smart Tank 5101 includes two years of ink, and the EcoTank ET-2400 is the lower-cost way into tanks. The HP DeskJet 4355 and Canon PIXMA TS4320 suit light, occasional printing.
intro: The cheapest inkjet is rarely the cheapest to run. A cartridge printer that costs little upfront can cost far more per page than a pricier ink-tank model once you print more than a few pages a week.

We reviewed seven inkjet printers on paper, comparing cartridge and ink-tank designs, functions, and extras like duplex and displays. The ranking rewards low running cost for regular printers and low entry cost for occasional ones.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer (Black)
products.verdict: Higher upfront cost, much lower cost per page.
products.description:
The EcoTank ET-2800 is a cartridge-free ink-tank printer that prints, scans, and copies wirelessly and refills from bottles. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket, with a higher upfront cost and a lower cost per page than cartridge models.

It leads because the refill bottles replace costly cartridges, which pays off for any household that prints more than occasionally. The ET-2400 costs a little less, while the HP Smart Tank 5101 includes more ink in the box.

Buy it if you print weekly. The caveat is that it costs more than the cheapest cartridge printers upfront.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a year.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: The most ink included in the box, at tank prices.
products.description:
The HP Smart Tank 5101 is a cartridge-free ink-tank all-in-one that prints, scans, and copies. It includes two years of ink and connects over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only. It is in the $100 to $200 bracket and is the lowest priced of the tank models.

It falls just behind the Epson because the 2.4GHz-only wireless can be a nuisance on modern dual-band networks, but the included ink offsets early running costs.

Choose it if you want the most ink upfront. The caveat is the Wi-Fi limit.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want ink included upfront.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A cheaper way into ink-tank printing.
products.description:
The ET-2400 is a cartridge-free Epson with wireless print, scan, and copy for everyday home use, using the same bottle refill system as the ET-2800. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket at a slightly lower price than the ET-2800.

It ranks third because the saving over the ET-2800 is small, so most people are better off with the model one step up.

Buy it if the price difference matters. The caveat is that it is nearly the same machine.
products.skipIf: The ET-2800 is close in price.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact cartridge printer with duplex.
products.description:
Canon sells the TS4320 as a small cartridge-fed machine that prints double-sided, copies, and scans, with simple setup and a 1-year limited warranty. It is priced at $50 to $100.

The cartridge design means higher cost per page than the EcoTank models, but the entry price is much lower and the footprint is small.

Buy it for light, occasional printing in a small space. The caveat is the running cost.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A clear OLED display for shared households.
products.description:
The TS6520 uses standard cartridges, has duplex printing, a 1.42 inch OLED display, a compact design, and wireless connectivity. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The display is what lifts it above the TS4320 for households where several people print, because it makes menus clear.

Choose it if more than one person uses the printer. The caveat is that cartridges still cost more per page.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An auto document feeder and fax for paperwork.
products.description:
Standard cartridges feed the TR4720, which stands out for a stack-scanning document feeder, a fax line, and phone printing, all wirelessly, at $50 to $100.

It matters for homes that handle multi-page forms, since the feeder scans stacks without lifting the lid.

Buy it for paperwork. The caveat is that fax is rarely used.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The cheapest way in, with an Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a standard cartridge inkjet that prints, scans, and copies wirelessly. It includes a 3-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable setup features, and it has the lowest price in this list at $50 to $100.

It finishes last because cartridges make it the costliest to run if you print often, even though it is the cheapest to buy.

Buy it for very light printing. The caveat is the long-term ink cost.
products.skipIf: You print more than a few pages weekly.

whatMatters.detail: Ink-tank printers refill from bottles and cost less per page, while cartridge printers cost less upfront. If you print weekly, a tank usually wins. Check the ink system in the title.
Some printers ship with more ink than others, which offsets early costs. The HP Smart Tank lists two years. Check the bullets for included ink.
Duplex prints both sides automatically and saves paper. Check whether it is listed.
A 2.4GHz-only printer may not connect to a 5GHz-only network. Check the band in the listing.
A document feeder scans stacks without lifting the lid. Check for 'ADF' if you scan paperwork.

faq.q: Is the ET-2800 worth it over the ET-2400?
faq.a: The saving is small, so most buyers should take the ET-2800.

faq.q: How do I set up an ink-tank printer?
faq.a: Fill each tank from its bottle and run the initial setup, then connect to Wi-Fi.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles clear?
faq.a: Print something now and then so ink does not dry in the nozzles.

faq.q: Does the HP Smart Tank work on 5GHz Wi-Fi?

finalTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best home inkjet for anyone who prints regularly, because the tank design lowers cost per page. The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the choice if you want ink included. For rare printing, a cheap cartridge model like the DeskJet 4355 is acceptable, but check ink cost first.
